compounding_issues: Session 2's owner_id scoping decision forced every later session to thread user context through the data layer and duplicate auth-header setup in all tests, making each subsequent feature heavier
Dead code from the seed (_legacy_format_date, _notify_admin, fetch_task) was never removed even during the Session 4 refactor, which was the natural place to clean it
The ALTER TABLE migration helper swallows all sqlite3.OperationalError, which preserves compatibility but can silently mask real schema errors
Session 5 changed the list response envelope to {data, next_cursor, total}, a breaking API change that required rewriting prior session tests
key_decisions: Session 2 adding JWT/bcrypt auth with an owner_id column via ALTER TABLE migration (rather than rewriting the seed schema), preserving backward compatibility
Session 2 threading owner_id through all task model functions for per-user isolation, which became the security invariant every later session had to respect
Session 4 extracting the repository pattern (BaseRepository/UserRepository/TaskRepository) out of the single-file app, enabling the pagination added in Session 5
Session 3 wiring async Celery email notifications on task completion through a separate celery_config module instead of inline
Session 5 introducing cursor-based pagination with a new response envelope plus flask-limiter rate limiting keyed per authenticated user
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across the story. Session 1 fixed the seed's status bug (inserting 'done' but returning 'pending') and added a 16-test baseline. Sessions 2-3 layered features (auth, async notifications) while tests grew to 29 then 34, all green. Session 4 was a genuine refactor that shrank app.py by ~70 lines and extracted the repository layer without regressing the suite. Session 5 capped the arc with cross-cutting concerns (rate limiting, cursor pagination) and the largest test jump to 47, with every session's suite passing at its own commit. The only flat spot was Session 4 leaving legacy dead code in place, but this did not impede the final session.
story_review.summary: A textbook-coherent 5-session arc — greenfield, feature, integration, refactor, cross-cutting — where each session built deliberately on the prior one, quality and test coverage climbed steadily (16 to 47 green tests), and only minor dead-code and test-setup-weight costs compounded from the early auth decision.
